text:
Linus Ullmark spent three weeks on injured reserve, came back on Nov. 12, and two nights later picked up the 200th win of his career in Pittsburgh. The bigger news is how good he has been when healthy. Through 10 starts he is 8-1-0 with a .939 save rate, and he has saved 9.4 goals above expected, which means he has kept out 9.4 more goals than the shots he faced would usually allow. That ranks in the 96th percentile among goalies.

This is a sharp turn from last season, when he finished 13.3 goals below expected in 49 games. He is winning on the easy shots and the hard ones alike: a .792 save rate on high-danger chances against a league .685. Ten starts is a small sample, and goalie numbers swing hard over short stretches, so we'd treat this as a strong start rather than a verdict. Ottawa sent Jonas Johansson to the AHL to make room for his return, which tells you whose net this is again.
